findings.title: §4.6 phrasing implies adultLinkedTo authorizes reading an un-accepted email invitee
findings.where: §4.6 ("allowed because a link exists") and §7.1 listMyStudents
findings.problem: The §4.6 bullet reads as if the adult can users-read every listed student, but adultLinkedTo only covers the deterministic studentUid_adultUid id. Un-accepted email invites (studentUid:null) have no such link; listMyStudents already handles this by displaying the typed email instead of a users read, so behavior is correct — only the phrasing is ambiguous.
findings.fix: Add a half-sentence to the §4.6 bullet clarifying the users-read is allowed only for rows with a concrete studentUid (userid invites, code-requests, accepted email invites), matching the helper comment already present in §6.

findings.title: Two pre-change anchors drift ~15-18 lines
findings.where: §4.5/§7.1 saveProfile (~659 vs actual ~654); §7.1 USERS/USERNAMES constants (~565 vs actual ~547-548)
findings.problem: Minor line-anchor drift. Both are trivially locatable by name and the doc instructs locate-by-name, so this does not block.
findings.fix: Tighten saveProfile anchor to ~654 and the collection-constants anchor to ~547 on the next edit.

findings.title: Inconsistent rule-helper style (let-binding vs inlined path)
findings.where: §6 approvedLinkExists/acceptableInviteExists use `let path = ...`; adultLinkedTo inlines the path
findings.problem: Purely stylistic; rules-v2 supports let bindings in functions and both forms are correct.
findings.fix: Optionally make the path-construction style uniform across helpers.
